questions: Is the reversal operation a global toggle that persists until reversed again, or does it only affect the current step and then the graph reverts?
Can you reverse the direction of all edges multiple times, and if so, is there any limit or cost each time?
Does moving along a directed edge require that the edge exists in the current orientation of the graph at that moment?
If you are at vertex N, do you stop immediately, or must you perform an operation that lands exactly on N?
Is the reversal operation allowed at any vertex, including vertex N?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, does moving along them count as a move with cost 1?
Is the graph guaranteed to be simple (no multiple edges between same ordered pair)?
Does the reversal operation flip all edges simultaneously, including those just traversed or to be traversed?
